text:
sasha-sre: alert: runtime-policy detected a pod with privileged=true + hostPath(/proc) mounted on prod-node-5. image: registry.redwood/cust-service:2.7.1, image sha reported by kubelet != registry digest, flagged as potential image tampering. markings: high - suspicious privileges. attaching container/daemon logs shortly.

amanda.dev: copy that. pod name? node? any svcaccount attached?

sasha-sre: pod: cust-service-5f8d7
node: prod-node-5
ns: payments
sa: payments-reader
containers: cust-service (privileged: true, hostPath: /proc readOnly:false)
kubelet log snippet: `pulled image sha: sha256:abcd1234...; registry manifest digest: sha256:efgh5678...`

ricardo.sec: yikes. mark as incident. immediate containment: 1) cordon prod-node-5 2) evict/kill pod 3) rotate tokens for payments-reader SA 4) snapshot node disk for forensics 5) restrict access to KMS keys used by service if any. Can someone run these? :warning:

otis-infra: doing cordon + drain now (will avoid full reboot). will create ephemeral snapshot of /var/lib/docker + containerd logs.

deploy-bot: note: there was a deploy pipeline for payments yesterday 22:14 UTC (pipeline #3145) by amanda.dev. image push event to registry at 22:06 UTC.

amanda.dev: I triggered that deploy. image build pipeline logs show digest sha256:efgh5678... pushed to registry. local build machine reported sha256:abcd1234... hmm looks inconsistent. I will stop any further deploys and revoke deploy token.

ricardo.sec: @kms-bot can you check KMS access logs for keys used by image signing/registry push and any unusual requests in the timeframe? Also pull registry audit (who pulled/pushed).

kms-bot: KMS logs: key image-sig-key used at 2026-07-10T22:05:57Z by ci-runner-12 from IP 10.40.3.9. No external KMS anomalies. Registry audit: push event at 2026-07-10T22:06:12Z from ci-runner-12; pull events afterwards from staged deploy runners and prod nodes. No third-party pulls recorded.

ricardo.sec: ok, still possible that build agent had corrupt/cached layers or CI compromised. Next: 1) revoke CI runner credentials 2) rotate image signing key 3) mark image as untrusted in registry; re-pull canonical image from CI after verification.

otis-infra: cordon+evict done. pod terminated, kubelet reported OOM when stopping but pod is gone. node isolated (no new pods scheduled). snapshotting now. collecting /var/log/kubelet.log, containerd logs, syscalls trace from auditd.

amanda.dev: I pulled pipeline artifacts and re-built the image locally with same Dockerfile, got digest sha256:efgh5678... I think the builder produced two different layers locally vs CI cache. Not yet evidence of tamper, could be nondeterministic build. But hostPath+privileged is unexpected for this service — where did that come from? my K8s manifest has no privileged flag.

sasha-sre: I found an admission webhook override for namespace payments in the last 24h — a patch job by ci-runner-12 changed podsecurity to allow_privileged for payments ns. audit log shows `kubectl patch` at 2026-07-10T22:09:01Z by ci-runner-12.

ricardo.sec: that is the pivot. CI runner had permissions to patch namespace RBAC. escalate: 1) revoke that runner's SA and tokens 2) rotate any cluster-admin tokens used by CI 3) run RBAC audit for similar privileges on other runners 4) add immediate policy blocking namespace-level privilege relaxation.

pagerduty: incident created: INC-2026-0710-42. priority P1. notify legal & infosec.

amanda.dev: taking responsibility to scrub my pipeline configs. will lock down pipeline service accounts and remove unnecessary RBAC. will add an explicit admission check for privileged in manifests.

ricardo.sec: post-containment checklist (short):
- forensic snapshot stored in secure bucket (link hidden)
- revoke CI runner creds + rotate KMS key used for signatures
- rotate SA tokens for payments-reader + any admin tokens used by CI
- add registry block/quarantine for affected image tag
- enforce image signature verification at admission controller
- add alert: mismatch between kubelet reported sha and registry manifest digest
- run vulnerability scan for any altered layers

otis-infra: adding a PodSecurity admission policy to deny privileged & hostPath for payments ns and others. rolling out cluster-wide deny-by-default in staging first.

amanda.dev: will create ticket to fix build determinism and add signed reproducible builds. also will add a test that compares local digest vs pushed digest.

ricardo.sec: timeline notes: root cause likely CI runner had excessive namespace/patch rights and used that to relax admission controls, which allowed a privileged pod with hostPath. image sha mismatch may be build nondeterminism rather than tamper, but treat as compromise until proven otherwise.

sasha-sre: thanks all. next actions: consolidate evidence in INC-2026-0710-42, run postmortem with remediation list, assign owners. please add any logs/artifacts to incident thread. :thumbsup:
